summary: phaser/ is a 566-file, ~32K-LOC (22,094 src + 7,927 tests + 2,664 scripts) Vite+React19+Phaser4+Zustand+Zod project with 9 runtime deps and 31 devDeps, of which 3 runtime deps are dead weight (framer-motion and howler have ZERO importers; react-aria hooks pkg has one) and an entire Storybook stack (8 devDeps, 3 stories, 8.3MB static output) has no bug-catching evidence since 2026-05-10. The tooling that demonstrably earned its keep is small and portable: the headless CLI (scripts/cli/play.ts+combat.ts+render.ts, 843 LOC) that drives the real stores and whose stalemate metric exposed the three engine bugs behind "balance" story 475; the 5 ESLint invariants (Math.random ban, dispatch chokepoint, three layer-import fences); lint-content.ts; the unmasked Playwright visual/boot/second-battle specs; and the multi-round reducer tests written after the AP-never-resets P0 slipped past 527 green unit tests. Current health: tsc green on both configs, vitest 590/590 in 14.9s, eslint RED with 18 errors (16 from react-hooks v7 set-state-in-effect/refs) and therefore excluded from `npm run verify`; there is no CI at all (no .github). The biggest debt is not tooling but superseded systems still on disk: the entire Oregon-Trail overworld strip UI (~3.5K LOC + ~12MB backdrops/dual-grid tiles) is obsolete under the 2026-08 "one open sheet" decision, there are three overlapping tile/terrain pipelines, and a rejected hand-pixel sprite toolkit (273 LOC + 4 scripts + 11 JSONs + 9 dead PNGs) is still wired into npm scripts. 32.8MB of binary assets are tracked in git (18 unit originals at 832x1216, a 1.96MB tile-demo output, an identical duplicate backdrop). The branded-ID system costs 352 `as unknown as` casts in src; BoardScene.ts (1,240 LOC), App.tsx (627 LOC, 39 commits), and runStore.ts (684 LOC, 45 action cases) are god files; five seed*Battle files duplicate placement logic (the dungeon one forgot to place the party, a P1). Critically, the newest and best pipeline (autotile.ts, boardFloor.ts, map-tool.ts, bake-board-sprites.ts, public/art/terrain/px/, tools/map-builder.html) is UNCOMMITTED in the working tree while CONTEXT.md already documents it as shipped; the rebuilder must harvest from the working tree, not HEAD. CONTEXT.md (279 lines, 32KB) plus its grep-based drift checker is a maintenance tax that scans only 4 of the 5 dirs its own protocol names and passes on any substring mention.

requirements.text: Math.random() is lint-banned project-wide (no-restricted-properties); all randomness threads an RNG parameter; sub-RNGs via deriveRng(parent, label) with Mulberry32 and a saved counter that fast-forwards on createRng so save/resume continues the same stream.

Store mutation goes through a single dispatch(action) chokepoint per store; ESLint no-restricted-syntax forbids useRunStore/useCombatStore/useMetaStore.setState outside src/state/** (tests/stories exempt). Storybook decorators currently violate this (src/storybook/decorators.tsx) — do not reintroduce that exemption.

Layer fences enforced by no-restricted-imports: src/ui/** may not import phaser or raw react-aria(-components); src/game/** may not import react/react-dom; src/systems/** and src/procgen/** may not import phaser/react/react-dom. Keep these three fences even if the UI library changes.

Dev server pinned to port 5183 with strictPort:true; Playwright baseURL defaults to http://localhost:5183 with PW_BASE_URL override and reuseExistingServer only when !CI. Port 5173 belongs to another app on this machine and reuseExistingServer would silently test it.

requirements.text: Fixed 1280x720 authored stage, CSS transform-scaled and letterboxed by a GameStage wrapper; position:fixed descendants resolve against the stage; overlays (modal/tooltip/popover) must portal INTO the stage container; after each rescale call game.scale.refresh() so canvas input stays mapped; Playwright viewport is 1280x720 with reducedMotion:'reduce'.

A headless CLI must drive the REAL stores + pure systems via tsx with no browser: interactive REPL (play/move/select/targets/auto/end/show/state), scripted --seed N --cmds 'a; b' --json, piped stdin, --autobattle --runs N with first-blood-gated stalemate detection (150-round cap, 12 stale rounds), --report --seeds N --loadout matrix ('none|default|roy=iron_sword+iron_buckler'), --scenario stub|dungeon:<id>:<room>|boss, and a dialogue walker. Combat log derived by diffing unit state.

The CLI combat engine must be importable as a library so golden-scenario Vitest tests (determinism: same seed => same outcome + turn count; engagement: HP actually drops; termination: autoBattle always ends) run in npm test.

Every turn/round/cycle system must have a test that runs >=3 FULL cycles and asserts per-turn restoration invariants each cycle (AP reset, hand refill to 5, discard reshuffle with no card loss, status expiry). Single-transition tests cannot see these; the beta shipped an AP-never-resets P0 past 527 unit + 22 e2e green tests.

Treat a 100%-stalemate or 0%-win sim result as an ENGINE smoke alarm before touching balance numbers: reproduce one battle by hand and verify damage lands, enemies close distance, and both sides are on the board (corpse shadowing, axis-only stepToward, unpositioned dungeon party were all sim 'stalemates'). The greedy sim AI is a FLOOR; validate tuning against manual play.

Visual snapshot tests must be UNMASKED with tight tolerance (maxDiffPixelRatio 0.0005), deterministic seed + reducedMotion, fonts.ready awaited; never mask the canvas/container (previous baselines were solid-magenta blanks that could never fail). Also assert zero console errors on boot per scene and no horizontal overflow past the stage.

requirements.text: The canvas container must be permanently mounted and visibility-toggled, never unmounted between views; an e2e test must run TWO battles in one page session and assert the canvas is attached and the scene display list is populated (>50 children) both times.

Dev-only test contract: ?view=combat|overworld|town|dungeon|camp fast-path seeds a representative run (party via buildStarterParty + 80 gold + 5 food, no prologue) and window.__debug exposes the stores (getState/dispatch), busRefs and diag; window.__game exposes the Phaser game. E2E resolves battles through the sanctioned dispatch (playCard with a 999-damage inline card + animationsCompleted), not by canvas clicking. Board clicks in e2e compute canvas coords from the SAME boardGeometry the game uses (tileSize/gridOriginX/Y), never hardcoded.

Green tests are not evidence of a working turn loop: 527 unit + 22 e2e were green when AP never reset after round 1 (a58fe8d), and the sim reported 90-100% stalemates for two months that were three engine bugs (f4c4bef). Write multi-cycle tests first and hand-play a battle before trusting any sim number.

The visual snapshot suite was silently useless for months: masks painted the whole 1280x720 frame magenta so three byte-identical baselines could never fail (7aaadf4). Never mask the container; verify a deliberate colour change actually fails the suite.
Port 5183 vs 5173: Playwright's reuseExistingServer will happily test whatever other app is on the port; pin strictPort and check what a port serves before debugging e2e (lesson_port_5173_collision).

Branded IDs (17 types in domain/ids.ts) fight Record<string,T> keys and yielded 352 `as unknown as` casts in src (BoardScene 65, combatReducer 39, runStore 28, enemyAI 20) plus 28 in the CLI. Either use plain string ids with runtime validation, or make the maps keyed by the branded type from the start — do not carry the cast pattern over.

Zod .parse strips undeclared keys: the real save->load path silently dropped daysElapsed/runStats/oneShotsFired for weeks because serializeRun wrote fields the schema did not declare (f120373). Use .strict() or a round-trip test over the real load path.

Designed-but-never-wired systems fooled every reader: eventBus.emit had zero call sites (quest listeners were dead data), hop RNG never advanced, captureTargets was read by nothing, validateContent is test-only, metaStore is never persisted, QuestEffect recruitUnit/spawnNode/unlockNode are no-op stubs. In the rebuild, a feature is not done until a test or the CLI exercises its emit/call site.

Storybook decorators mutate stores via setState (src/storybook/decorators.tsx), exempted from the chokepoint lint — any playground you add must go through dispatch or it will diverge from real state shapes.

react-hooks ESLint v7 introduced set-state-in-effect/refs rules that produced 16 new errors; lint was then dropped from `verify` rather than fixed. Pin plugin versions and put lint in the gate on day one, or the gate rots the same way.

The unit-test suite spends 237s cumulative in jsdom environment setup for 14.9s of wall time; UI component tests dominate. Keep DOM tests for modal FLOWS only (PartyLoadout, Dialogue, PauseMenu) and keep pure-system tests environment: node.

32.8MB of PNGs are tracked in git (118 files) and 41MB more sit untracked in public/sprites/lab; the repo will bloat with every art iteration. Use Git LFS or keep originals outside the repo and commit only the board bakes + portraits actually referenced by data/unitSprites.ts.

Decide up front whether a 1.2MB framework is worth it for that — if kept, keep BoardScene split (grid/overlays/units/effects/enemy-driver are five classes crammed into one file, 42 commits of churn).

App.tsx (627 LOC, 39 commits) is simultaneously router, battle seeder, save orchestrator, audio controller, tutorial gate and dev seeder; runStore.ts is a 45-case switch. The rebuild needs a thin shell + per-feature slices or the same god files reappear within a month.

tools/map-builder.html is a 941KB single-file app with 408 base64-embedded tiles; the palette must stay byte-identical to public/art/terrain/px/ or autotile keys break. Generate it from px/ rather than hand-editing.

Specs are append-only and now number 15 (~380KB) + 17 plans + 20 research docs; CONTEXT.md is capped at 300 lines but is 32KB of dense prose. The doc surface has become larger than the code an agent needs to read — the rebuild should ship ONE short architecture README and let the typed contracts + lint fences carry the invariants.
